outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the DPH plan check application in parallel with the building permit application, including scaled drawings, a menu, and equipment specifications. What to say: Apply online at sfdph.org/ehsportal with the BAN, a Location ID number (LIN, assigned when you register the business), and the federal EIN. Submit two sets of scaled plans showing the kitchen layout, all sinks (three-compartment, hand, prep, mop), equipment, finishes (sealed surfaces, FRP wall panels), and the grease interceptor. Include a proposed menu. The flat fee for a new restaurant plan check is $2,207 (8 hours, FY2026–27); extra review is billed at $276/hour. Schedule a pre-final inspection at roughly 80% construction completion and a final inspection at least two weeks before opening.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the ABC Type 41 licence after the CUA is approved, or begin a licence transfer escrow if acquiring an existing licence. What to say: If applying for a new Type 41: file the application with ABC online or by mail, including a copy of the signed lease, the CUA approval, the seller's permit, the entity formation documents, and the $1,000 original licence fee. Post the ABC public notice at the premises for 30 days. ABC refers the application to SFPD and SF Planning; Planning's referral response will cite the CUA and the § 202.2(a) conditions. Expect 60–120 days if unprotested; census tract 208.02 is over-concentrated (22 active on-sale licences against 10 authorised), so ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the Board of Supervisors, adding 1–3 months. If transferring a licence: engage an ABC licence broker to locate a Type 41, negotiate the purchase price, open escrow, and file the transfer application; transfers also require the 30-day posting and city sign-offs.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Install a grease interceptor and submit the FOG Installation Verification Form to SF Public Utilities Commission. What to say: SFPUC inspectors assign a Discharger Category (1, 2 or 3) based on the kitchen's grease load; the category dictates the type and size of interceptor required under the Fats, Oils & Grease Control Ordinance. Install the interceptor during the tenant improvement construction and submit the Installation Verification Form to SFPUC after the plumbing final; this earns a 14.2% reduction on the sewer portion of the utility bill. An undersized or missing interceptor will cause DBI to withhold final sign-off.
outcomes.note: Record does not state the category is based on grease load, the specific timing relative to tenant improvement or plumbing final, or that missing interceptor will (certainly) cause withholding.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Complete the health permit application and schedule the DPH final inspection; obtain RBS and food handler certifications for all staff. What to say: After the DPH plan check is approved and construction is substantially complete, apply for the Health Permit to Operate online with the BAN and LIN. Pay the $470 application fee (includes the initial inspection). Ensure at least one owner or employee has passed an ANSI-accredited food safety manager exam (ServSafe, Prometric, etc., $100–$250, valid 5 years) and the certificate is on site. All employees who handle food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire ($7–$15 online, 2-hour course). All alcohol servers and their managers must complete ABC RBS training within 60 days of hire ($3 ABC portal registration plus $10–$25 course). Schedule the final DPH inspection; the inspector confirms the facility matches the approved plans and all equipment is in place. The permit is issued after the inspection passes.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $6,500 to $22,000. Notes: The timeline of 120–300 days and government cost of $6,500–$22,000 cover the Conditional Use Authorization, health permit to operate, and building permit with change of use when those approvals are granted. The range reflects: CUA hearing scheduling (120–180 days from filing to approval, based on the 2018–2019 comparables at 192 m and cases within 1,000 ft that took 6 months), building permit plan review and inspections (14–120 days depending on plan completeness and whether a change of occupancy is confirmed), and DPH plan check and inspections (21–60 days). ABC Type 41 licence processing (60–120 days per the catalog) is not included in the day or cost totals because the alcohol licence row's status is insufficient information; if a new Type 41 is required and the census tract's undue concentration triggers a Public Convenience or Necessity finding, add 1–3 months and the ABC $1,000–$1,600 licence fee. Costs shown are government permit and inspection fees only: CUA application approximately $3,150, DPH plan check $828–$2,207 (depending on scope), health permit application $470 (plus $0 annual licence fee for restaurants in FY2026–27), building permit $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction valuation), business registration $55–$95 (for a new small business), entity formation $70–$150, and miscellaneous items (FOG, sign permit, seller's permit, EDD, workers' comp setup) $0–$2,000. The timeline does not account for a denial or a withdrawal; it is a time to approval. Construction, architecture, legal, and licence broker fees are not government costs and are not included.

Notes: The timeline of 120–300 days and government cost of $6,500–$22,000 cover the Conditional Use Authorization, health permit to operate, and building permit with change of use when those approvals are granted. The range reflects: CUA hearing scheduling (120–180 days from filing to approval, based on the 2018–2019 comparables at 192 m and cases within 1,000 ft that took 6 months), building permit plan review and inspections (14–120 days depending on plan completeness and whether a change of occupancy is confirmed), and DPH plan check and inspections (21–60 days). ABC Type 41 licence processing (60–120 days per the catalog) is not included in the day or cost totals because the alcohol licence row's status is insufficient information; if a new Type 41 is required and the census tract's undue concentration triggers a Public Convenience or Necessity finding, add 1–3 months and the ABC $1,000–$1,600 licence fee. Costs shown are government permit and inspection fees only: CUA application approximately $3,150, DPH plan check $828–$2,207 (depending on scope), health permit application $470 (plus $0 annual licence fee for restaurants in FY2026–27), building permit $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction valuation), business registration $55–$95 (for a new small business), entity formation $70–$150, and miscellaneous items (FOG, sign permit, seller's permit, EDD, workers' comp setup) $0–$2,000. The timeline does not account for a denial or a withdrawal; it is a time to approval. Construction, architecture, legal, and licence broker fees are not government costs and are not included.
outcomes.note: The cited catalogs show individual permit times (CUA comparables 169-176 days, building 14-120 days, DPH 21-60 days) and some fees (DPH $828-$2,207, health permit $470, building $800-$15,000), but not the combined 120-300 day or $6,500-$22,000 ranges, nor CUA fees, entity formation costs, or miscellaneous item costs.
